newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria basic food prices ease 0.2 pct May 1-10.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria basic food prices ease 0.2 pct May 1-10.

text.p: Prices of the 38 most traded foods in Bulgaria fell 0.2 percent on average in the first 10 days of May and the monthly inflation rate was expected to be low, a National Statistics Institute (NSI) official said on Wednesday.
"Monthly inflation for May is likely to be low as food prices continue to decline after falling by 3.9 percent last month," the official, who declined to be named, told Reuters.

Monthly inflation slowed to below zero in April for the first time since Bulgaria launched market reforms in 1990 and the NSI began measuring inflation, mainly due to the lev rise and improved macroeconomic performance.
Prices of some types of bread fell by between 0.6 and 1.1 percent in the first 10 days of May while other types were 1.8 percent more expensive, the official said.
Meat prices rose by 2.9 percent on average due to a fodder grain shortage.

The interim cabinet recently liberalised food and fuel prices in line with recommendations made by the International Monetary Fund prior to introduction of a fixed exchange rate regime, but prices have not risen as the lev has traded stable near 1,500 to the dollar since the beginning of the month.
